# lrmodel

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/diggsm/bios625_hw4/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/diggsm/bios625_hw4/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/diggsm/bios625_hw4/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/diggsm/bios625_hw4)
<!-- badges: end -->

The `lrmodel` package was designed to re-implement the base R function `lm()`. 
The package contains two core functions functions: `lrmodel()` generate results 
from a linear regression model, and `lrmodel_summary()` produces a formatted 
summary of the results.

## Installation

You can install the development version of lrmodel from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("diggsm/bios625_hw4")
```

## Usage

Below are examples of how to use the `lrmodel` package to fit a simple linear 
regression model and explore the results.

```{r}
#| label: example
library(lrmodel)

# Fitting a simple linear regression model
model <- lrmodel(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)
model$coefficients

model$call

summary(model$residuals)

model$rank

# View a formatted summary of the linear regression model results
lrmodel_summary(model)
```


```{r}
#| label: fitted.vals
# Plotting the fitted values
plot(
  x = mtcars$mpg, y = model$fitted.values,
  xlab = "Miles per Gallon (mtcars)",
  ylab = "Miles per Gallon (lrmodel)"
  )
abline(a = 0, b = 1, col = "red")
```

```{r}
#| label: residuals
# Plotting the residuals
plot(
  x = mtcars$wt,
  y = model$residuals,
  xlab = "Weight (1000 lbs)",
  ylab = "Residuals"
)
abline(a = 0, b = 0, lty = 2)
```
